                        Γ.Scales
                           .Visual or Verbal Analogue Scale
                              • Scales of 0-10 for dizziness are helpful to determine if persons with vestibular disorders become symptomatic during their exercises
                                 00 - no symptoms
                                 010 - worst symptoms that they have ever experienced (need to go to the emergency room)

                                 1. 0 - No symptoms
                                 2. 1–3 - Mild
                                 3. 4–6 - Moderate
                                 4. 7–9 - Severe
                                 5. 10 - Worst symptoms that they have ever experienced (need to go to the emergency room)
                           .('')
                              1. Please choose from 0 to 10 corresponding to your perceived difficulty of each exercise:
                                  - 0: Extremely easy
                                  - 1: Easy
                                  - 2: Easy
                                  - 3: Somewhat easy
                                  - 4: Somewhat easy
                                  - 5: Somewhat hard
                                  - 6: Somewhat hard
                                  - 7: Hard
                                  - 8: Hard
                                  - 9: Extremely hard
                                  - 10: Extremely hard

                              2. Please choose from A to E corresponding to your perceived difficulty of each exercise:
                                  - A: I feel completely steady
                                  - B: I feel a little unsteady or off-balance
                                  - C: I feel somewhat unsteady or like I may lose my balance
                                  - D: I feel very unsteady or like I definitely will lose my balance
                                  - E: I lost my balance
                        .CPG for Peripheral Vestibular Hypofunction - Γ Vestibular Rehabilitation for Peripheral Vestibular Hypofunction: Updated Clinical Practice Guideline Guideline Development Group
                           .Action Statement 6
                              -Action statement 6a: optimal balance exercise dose in the treatment of individuals with peripheral vestibular hypofunction (unilateral and bilateral)
                                  -Clinicians may prescribe static and dynamic exercises for a minimum of:
                                      • No specific dosage recommendations for individuals with acute/subacute unilateral hypofunction at this time
                                      • 20 minutes daily for at least 4-6 weeks for individuals with chronic unilateral hypofunction
                                      • 20 minutes daily for 6-9 weeks for individuals with bilateral vestibular hypofunction
                                      • Evidence quality: II; Recommendation strength: weak/expert opinion
                     .Adaptation
                        .Vestibular Adaptation
                            • Induced by retinal slip, i.e., movement of visual images across the retina
                            • Retinal slip results in an error signal that the brain attempts to minimize 
                            • Over time, there is a rebalancing of the firing rate in the vestibular nuclei
                                • Reducing the asymmetry
                                • Increasing the VOR gain
                        .Principles of the Adaption Approach
                            • CNS response to exercise takes time
                            • Adaptation is context specific - exercises should stress the system in different ways (frequency, position, direction)
                            • Encourage mental effort to improve response
                            • Patients should always work at their limit of ability
                        ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                        .Adaption Exercises: Gaze Stability Exercises
                           .Guidelines for Performing Adaptation Exercises
                              • Target must be clear when doing the exercise
                              • Head movement:
                                  • ~20- 30°
                                  • Must be smooth
                                  • Should be practiced horizontally & vertically
                              • Observe eye movements to make sure they are focused on the target
                              • Push upper limits of patient ability – find the “just right” challenge!
                              • Can use a metronome so that you have an idea of how fast they are moving
                              • Goal: 1-2 minute of continuous gaze stability exercise 4-6 times/day
                           .(the exercises)------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                              • X1 viewing exercises (VORx1):
                                  • Head moving while visually fixating on a stationary target
                                  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                     .Adaption Exercises: X1 viewing
                                       • Hold or place a business card with a letter (i.e., hold an “X” at arms length or tape to the wall)
                                       • Turn head side to side or up and down 20 – 300 in either direction
                                       • Maintain clear and stable target
                                  .X1 Viewing Exercise: Complex Background ('')
                              • VORx1 with vergence:
                                  • Head moving while visually fixating on a target moving toward the nose
                                  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                    .Increasing the VOR gain
                                        • Do VORx1 with vergence 
                              • X2 viewing exercises (VORx2):
                                  • Head moving while visually fixating on a moving target
                                  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                    .Adaption Exercises: X2 viewing
                                        • Hold a business card with a letter (i.e., an “X” at arms length)
                                        • Turn head side to side or up and down 10-15 degrees in either direction while moving the target in the opposite direction
                                        • Maintain clarity of target
                           .Progression of Adaptation Exercises
                              I. Duration  
                               A. 1 ➔ 2 minutes per exercise  

                              II. Frequency  
                               A. 2 ➔ 5 times per day  

                              III. Velocity  
                               A. Increase head speed while keeping target in focus  

                              IV. Target Size  
                               A. Large ➔ Small  

                              V. Target Distance  
                               A. Near ➔ Far  

                              VI. Background  
                               A. Simple ➔ Complex  

                              VII. Position of Patient  
                               A. Supported Sitting ➔ Walking  

                              VIII. Support Surface  
                               A. Firm ➔ Compliant  

                              IX. Stance  
                               A. Wide ➔ Narrow BOS
                           .CPG for Peripheral Vestibular Hypofunction - Γ Vestibular Rehabilitation for Peripheral Vestibular Hypofunction: Updated Clinical Practice Guideline Guideline Development Group
                              .Action Statement 6
                                 -Action statement 6B: optimal gaze stabilization exercise dosage of treatment in persons with peripheral vestibular hypofunction (unilateral or bilateral)
                                     -Clinicians may prescribe weekly clinic visits plus a home exercise program of gaze 
                                     stability exercises consisting of a minimum of:
                                         • 3 times per day for a total of at least 12 minutes per day for patients with acute/subacute vestibular hypofunction
                                         • 3-5 times per day for a total of at least 20 minutes per day for patients with chronic vestibular hypofunction
                                         • 3-5 times per day for a total of 20-40 minutes per day for approximately 5-7 weeks for individuals with bilateral vestibular hypofunction 
                                         • Evidence Quality: II; Recommendation Strength: weak
                     .Substitution
                        .Substitution Exercises for dizziness/oscillopsia
                            • Purpose: To foster the use of alternative strategies to replace the lost or compromised vestibular function (often bilateral loss)
                            • Goals:
                                Improve gaze stabilization
                                Maximize postural stability
                                Central preprogramming
                                Use of other strategies:
                                    Corrective eye saccades
                                    Slowed head movements
                                    Increase use of smooth pursuit
                        .Substitution Exercises
                            • Eye-Head Saccade Exercise
                                Facilitates use of saccadic or smooth pursuit strategies and central pre-programming
                                ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                    .Eye-Head Saccade Exercise
                                        • Hold two targets at eye level 25-30 cm apart, head in midline
                                        • Move eyes to one target
                                        • Maintain eyes on target and turn head to same target
                                        • Shift eyes to second target
                                        • Move head to second target
                                        • Repeat in opposite direction
                            • Remembered/Imaginary Targets
                                Improve voluntary control and central pre-programming
                                ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                .Remembered/Imaginary Targets
                                    • Place target directly in front of you (patient should not hold the target)
                                    • While looking at the target, close eyes
                                    • Slowly turn head away while imagining the target 
                                    • Open eyes and verify still focused on the target adjust gaze if necessary 
                                    • Repeat in multiple directions and at variable speeds
                                .General Progression of Substitution Exercises
                                    I. Duration  
                                     A. 1 ➔ 2 minutes per exercise  

                                    II. Frequency  
                                     A. 2 ➔ 5 times per day  

                                    III. Velocity  
                                     A. Increase head speed while keeping target in focus  

                                    IV. Target Size  
                                     A. Large ➔ Small  

                                    V. Target Distance  
                                     A. Near ➔ Far  

                                    VI. Background  
                                     A. Simple ➔ Complex  

                                    VII. Position of Patient  
                                     A. Supported sitting ➔ Walking  

                                    VIII. Support Surface  
                                     A. Firm ➔ Compliant  
                                     B. Wide ➔ Narrow BOS
                     .Habituation
                        .Habituation Exercises ('')
                            • Reduction of symptoms after repeated stimulation
                            • VOR cancellation can be used for habituation
                            • Virtual reality scenes and YouTube videos
                            .(the exercises)------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                              .Binocular vision abnormalities
                                 • Office-based therapy with home exercise program
                                     • Pencil push-ups
                                     • Brock string
                                 • If not responding to treatment – refer out
                              .Adjunct treatments and patient education
                                  • Diagnosis
                                  • Lifestyle recommendations
                                  • Treatment plan
                                  • HEP
                                  • Prognosis
                                  • Transition toward independence/back to regular activity and participation
                                  • Medications
                                  • Psychologically-informed techniques
                                  • Vision therapy
                                  • Incorporate other team members as appropriate

                                    ΓTests Γ(TESTS)
                                       Ia.Oculomotor Examination
                                          ΓGenerals
                                             (Γ).Why assess ocular alignment
                                                 • Provides a  baseline prior to an assessment of VOR and vestibular-specific tests
                                                 • Rule out red flags
                                                 • Better estimate prognosis
                                                 • Determine treatment strategies, specific interventions
                                                 • Identify appropriate referrals or need for concurrent treatments
                                             (Γ).Skew Deviation 1
                                                 • Vertical misalignment of the eye due to a central nervous system lesion
                                                 • Can be obvious with observation
                                                 • Identified with cross cover test
                                                     • Will see one eye move up and one eye move down
                                             (Γ).Oculomotor Testing
                                                • For all vestibular tests – measuring eye movements
                                                • Purpose – make sure eyes are working
                                                • Vertical and horizontal gaze (H test and gaze-evoked)
                                                    oProvides information about whether the person can fixate their eyes without nystagmus
                                                • Saccades
                                                • Smooth Pursuit
                                                • Optokinetic nystagmus
                                             (Γ)Oculomotor tests
                                                Since vestibular tests measure eye (mostly), need to make sure eyes are working
                                          ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                          .V1.Nine Quadrant Test
                                          .V2.Gaze Holding Nystagmus
                                             ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                             • Ocular ROM
                                                (Γ).Ocular range of motion
                                                    • Observe the eyes at rest 
                                                    • Ask your patient to look in all 9 quadrants
                                                        • Observe for range of movement
                                                        • Observe for alignment
                                                        • Observe for any nystagmus
                                                        • Observe for a drift back to the center position (impaired gaze holding)
                                                            • The patient will need to hold in eccentric gaze for up to 30 seconds
                                          .V3.Smooth Pursuit
                                             • Smooth pursuits
                                                (Γ).Smooth Pursuits
                                                    • Smooth pursuit eye movements are not affected by peripheral vestibular loss 
                                                    • Smooth pursuit movement is at <60°/s
                                                    • Pursuit eye movements enable the individual to visually pursue a moving object across the visual field without making compensatory head movements
                                                    • Damage to the smooth pursuit system is often caused by cerebellar lesions
                                                (Γ).Assessment of smooth pursuits
                                                   • Examiner should present a specific target (e.g., fingertip, point of a pen)
                                                   • The target should be about 3 feet from the patient
                                                   • The examiner should ask the patient to follow the target without moving their head
                                                   • The examiner should slowly move the target from side to side
                                                   • Important to note the smoothness and conjugacy of the eye movement
                                                       • Do the eyes move together?
                                                       • Do the eyes move smoothly?
                                                   • Repeat moving the target up and down
                                                   • Smooth pursuit dysfunction may appear saccadic or “choppy” and would indicate central (brain) involvement
                                          .V4.Horizontal and Vertical Saccades
                                             • Saccades
                                                (Γ).Saccades
                                                   • Saccadic eye movements are rapid voluntary movements that allow re-foveation of stationary targets 
                                                   • Move at 350-600°/sec
                                                   • Series of saccadic eye movements are used when we read
                                                   • Impaired function may be indicative of a central nervous system lesion
                                                (Γ).Assessment of saccades
                                                   • Examiner should use 2 specific targets (e.g., fingertips, pen tips)
                                                   • Targets should be about 3 feet from the target and oriented about 1.5 feet from midline to each side
                                                   • The examiner instructs the patient to move their eyes as quickly as possible from one target to the other (side to side) without moving their head
                                                   • Re-orient the targets vertically and repeat asking the patient to look up and down
                                                   • Examiner should note speed, conjugacy, latency, accuracy
                                                   • Abnormal findings include slow saccades, hypermetric (overshooting), or hypometric (undershooting), and/or restricted amplitude
                                                (Γ).Abnormal saccades often indicate central nervous system involvement
                                                   • Parkinson’s disease
                                                   • Progressive supranuclear palsy
                                                   • Intranuclear ophthalmoplegia
                                                   • Drug intoxication
                                                   • Olivopontocerebellar atrophy
                                                   • Huntington’s disease
                                                   • Cranial nerve 3, 4, 6 palsy
                                          .V5.Convergence
                                             (Γ).Vergence Γ(Este va ací?)¿?
                                                • Convergence
                                                    • Adduction of both eyes together allowing for binocular fixation on a target
                                                • Divergence
                                                    • Symmetrical abduction of both eyes as a visual target moves away from the face
                                             (Γ).Assessment of Vergence Γ(Este va ací?)¿?
                                                • Examiner asks the patient to focus on a target (14-point font) held at arms length
                                                • The patient should focus on the target as it is moved toward their nose
                                                • Measure near point of convergence
                                                    • Point at which the image doubles or eyes diverge
                                                    • Repeat at least 3 times and average
                                                • >5 cm is abnormal indicating convergence insufficiency
                                                • Convergence insufficiency is present in 35-55% of individuals after mild traumatic brain injury
                                                     • Cranial nerve 8: hearing screen, head impulse test/VOR assessment
                                                 • May also include a screen of other cranial nerves
                                          .V6.Cover and Uncover Test
                                             (Γ).Cover/Uncover Test Γ(Este va ací?)¿?
                                                 • Cover test: assessing for tropias
                                                 • Ask the patient to focus on a far target (approximately 10 feet)
                                                 • Cover one eye with an occluder
                                                 • Look for any movement in the opposite eye
                                                     • Movement in = exotropia
                                                     • Movement out = esotropia
                                                     • Movement up = hypotropia
                                                     • Movement down = hypertropia
                                                 • Repeat in opposite eye
                                                 • Normal alignment: no movement of either eye 
                                          .V7.Cross-Cover Test
                                             (Γ).Cross Cover Test 1 Γ(Este va ací?)¿?
                                                 • Cross cover test: assessing for phorias (if cover test was normal)
                                                     • Ask the patient to focus on a far target (approximately 10 feet)
                                                     • Cover one eye with an occulder 
                                                     • Hold for a few seconds then quickly move to cover the opposite eye and repeat
                                                     • Look for movement in the eye that is being uncovered (look at the occlude as you uncover the eye)
                                                         • Movement in = exophoria
                                                         • Movement out = esophoria
                                                         • Movement up/down = hyper/hypo-phoria
                                       Ib.Vestibular ocular reflex (VOR) testing
                                          .V8.Head Impulse Test (Horizontal Canal)
                                             • Cranial nerve 8: hearing screen, head impulse test/VOR assessment
                                                (See: '24 Vestibular Exam Part 1::Cranial nerve 8 auditory screening')
                                             ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                             .Head Impulse Test
                                                • Assessment of semicircular canal function (angular VOR)
                                                • Ask the patient to look at a target in midline (usually examiner’s nose)
                                                • The patient’s neck should be flexed about 30 degrees 
                                                • Grasp the head and rotate it slowly 15-20 degrees to the right or left and 
                                                then briskly return the head to the center
                                                • Head ‘impulse’ should be:
                                                • Small amplitude (5-15 degrees)
                                                • Moderate velocity (approximately 200 deg/sec)
                                                • High acceleration (3,000-4,000 deg/sec2)
                                                • Head impulse should be delivered with unpredictable timing and direction 
                                                for optimal sensitivity

                                             .Head Impulse Test considerations
                                                • Normal response: The patient should be able to focus on the central target 
                                                (eyes will move in the opposite direction of the head movement)
                                                • Vestibular loss: the VOR will not move the eyes as quickly as the head 
                                                rotation, causing a “corrective” saccade to re-fixate on the target
                                                • Unilateral vestibular hypofunction: corrective saccade will be present when 
                                                the head is rotated toward the side of the lesion
                                                • Bilateral vestibular hypofunction: corrective saccade will be present in both 
                                                directions
                                                • Sensitivity of the HIT for identifying vestibular hypofunction was 71% for 
                                                UVH and 84% for BVH
                                          .V9.HINTS Exam (V8.=HI=Head Impulse, V3.=N=Nystagmus, & V6.=TS=Test Skew)
                                             .Head Impulse Nystagmus Test of Skew (HINTS)
                                                 • Cluster of tests to help identify central causes from peripheral causes of acute 
                                                 dizziness
                                                 • Often used in ED settings among individuals with acute dizziness/vertigo with 
                                                 spontaneous nystagmus
                                                 ``• Among individuals with acute dizziness and spontaneous nystagmus, findings that indicate a central pathology include any of the following: (!!E)
                                                        • Presence of NORMAL head impulse test (HIT)
                                                        • Direction-changing nystagmus with gaze (gaze evoked nystagmus)
                                                        • Skew deviation with cover test
                                                 • Sensitivity 100%; Specificity 96% (more specific than early MRI)
                                          .V10.Head Shake Test (Head Shaking Nystagmus)
                                             .Head Shake Test 1
                                                • Can aid in diagnosis of a unilateral peripheral vestibular disorder
                                                • Vision should be occluded
                                                • The patient is instructed to close their eyes 
                                                • The examiner flexes the head by about 30 degrees and then 
                                                oscillates the head horizontally for 20 cycles at the frequency of 2 
                                                repetitions per second (2 Hz)
                                                • The patient is then asked to open their eyes
                                                • The examiner should observe for nystagmus

                                             .Head Shake Test 2
                                                • Normal response: no nystagmus present
                                                • Unilateral vestibular hypofunction: horizontal nystagmus with the 
                                                quick phase beating toward the healthy ear (slow phase toward the 
                                                lesioned ear)
                                                • Presence of vertical nystagmus post-head shaking could indicate a 
                                                central lesion
                                                • The nystagmus occurs because of the asymmetry of vestbulo-ocular 
                                                reflex (VOR) 
                                                • Positive findings have been related to the degree of caloric weakness
                                          .V11.Dynamic Visual Acuity Test
                                             .Dynamic Visual Acuity Test
                                                • A measure of visual acuity during horizontal motion of the head
                                                • Clinical version and instrumented (computerized) versions
                                                • First, the examiner should determine static visual acuity for the patient by 
                                                asking them to read an eye chart (identify the lowest complete line)
                                                • Then, the examiner rotates the patient’s head to the right and left at 2 
                                                cycles per second (2 Hz) while the patient reads the eye chart again
                                                • Identify the difference between static and visual acuity (how many lines 
                                                were lost with dynamic visual acuity)
                                                • Normal response: loss of 2 lines or less
                                                • A loss of greater than 2 lines is indicative of vestibular hypofunction
                                          ✗.V12.Vibration Induced Nystagmus
                                          ✗.V13.Rinne test Γ(V13. & V14. go togerther)
                                          ✗.V14.Weber test Γ(V13. & V14. go togerther)
                                          Γ✗[As an Assessment].CT2.VOR Cancellation (Visual Motion Sensitivity)
                                             .VOR Cancellation
                                                • We need to suppress the VOR sometimes during eye-head movement so that the image 
                                                can stay on the fovea
                                                • To assess, the patient should sit and focus on a target or thumb held at arm’s length
                                                • The head and body/arm should rotate together approximately 80 degrees to each side at 
                                                a comfortable speed 
                                                • The patient should maintain gaze on the target
                                                • Normal response: the eyes will maintain focus on the target
                                                • Abnormal response: presence of corrective saccades or inability to focus on the target 
                                                (indicates a central lesion)
                                                • Peripheral vestibular lesions will not lead to impaired VOR cancellation
                                                • However, patients with peripheral vestibular lesions may become symptomatic with this test

                                    III.Posterior Canal BPPV Positional Tests Γ(TESTS)
                                       Γ.Generals Γ(Algunes d'ací apliquen a tots els testos encara que h he posat en esta secció)
                                          .Preparation for BPPV assessment and treatment
                                              • Assess range of motion of the neck
                                              • Remove glasses
                                              • Remove large earrings, jewelry
                                              • Remove hats
                                              • Tuck in your tie
                                              • Ask about motion sensitivity/sickness
                                          .Conditions that require caution when performing the maneuvers
                                              • Cervical stenosis
                                              • Severe kyphoscoliosis
                                              • Limited cervical ROM
                                              • Down’s syndrome
                                              • Severe rheumatoid arthritis
                                              • Cervical radiculopathies
                                              • Ankylosing spondylitis
                                              • Low back dysfunction
                                              • Spinal cord injuries
                                              • Paget’s disease
                                              • Morbid obesity
                                              • Torn or detached retina
                                              • Glaucoma
                                              • Cognitive deficits
                                              • Unstable cardiac conditions
                                              When in doubt, get clearance from the physician
                                          .What should NOT be done to treat BPPV
                                              • Do not recommend radiographic testing (CT, MRI)
                                              • Do not recommend vestibular testing (caloric, VEMP, etc)
                                              • Do not prescribe vestibular suppressant medication
                                              • It will sedate the person but will not “fix” the BPPV
                                              • Do not provide strict instructions post-CRM
                                          .Falls and Vestibular Disorders
                                              • Falls occur more frequently in persons with vestibular disorders than older adults living in the community 
                                              • There is a 12-fold increase in reported falls in persons over the age of 40 who report dizziness
                                              ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                              .CRMs decrease falls among those with BPPV
                                                  • In one study 120 individuals received the Epley and were followed for 12 months 
                                                  • The reduction in the number of reported falls was statistically significant (398 falls in the 12 months prior to the maneuver vs 139 in the 12 months after the maneuver)
                                                  • In another study, 40 people over the age of 65 were referred to a falls clinic in the UK who had BPPV
                                                  • Prior to the CRM, all patients had experienced a fall in the past 6 months
                                                  • 6 months after the CRM, 30 out of the 40 patients experienced a fall
                                                  • There was a decrease from 128 to 46 falls which was a 64% decrease in reported falls
                                          .Why should you perform a CRM?
                                              • Your patients will love you
                                              • You can “fix” their problem with no medication/surgery (sometimes in one visit!)
                                              • It could prevent a fall
                                              • Your patient’s quality of life is enhanced
                                          .BPPV by canal type
                                             1. BPPV by canal type
                                                - Posterior
                                                  - Estimated frequency: 81–89%
                                                  - Provocative maneuver: Dix Hallpike
                                                  - Nystagmus: Upbeat, torsional
                                                - Horizontal
                                                  - Estimated frequency: 8–17%
                                                  - Provocative maneuver: Supine Roll Test (Pagnini-McClure)
                                                  - Nystagmus: Horizontal Direction Changing
                                                - Anterior
                                                  - Estimated frequency: 1–3%
                                                  - Provocative maneuver: Dix Hallpike
                                                  - Nystagmus: Downbeat, torsional
                                          .Positional Testing
                                             Static - not BPPV
                                             Tell you if something is wrong, but not where
                                             May distinguish between peripheral and central
                                             ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                             • Purpose: test effect of different head positions within the gravitational field
                                             • Slow movement into stationary position
                                                 oSitting
                                                     ▪ Head left & right
                                                 oSupine
                                                     ▪ Head straight, left, & right
                                                 oRight decubitus (side lying)
                                                 oLeft decubitus
                                                 oPre-caloric position
                                                     ▪ Head & shoulders elevated 30° from supine
                                          .Positional Nystagmus
                                             • Criteria for clinical significance 
                                                 oSlow Component Velocity (SCV) > 5 deg/s in any position
                                                 oSCV < 6 deg/s – persistent in 4+ positions
                                                 oSCV < 6 deg/s – sporadic in all positions
                                             • Interpretation
                                                 oSomething wrong with vestibular system – hard to localize
                                                 oDirection fixed all positions – probably peripheral
                                                 oDirection changing - central until proven otherwise
                                                 oNystagmus with visual fixation – probably central
                                          (Aplica a tot a partir d'ací)------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                          .Timing and repetition of CRMs
                                             • Gordon and Gadoth (2004) suggest that repeated repositioning within one session provides superior results to a single maneuver
                                             • Repetition of CRM depends on:
                                                 • Response to treatment
                                                 • Patient tolerance
                                                 • Time constraints
                                             • Timing between repetition may vary depending on patient response to treatment
                                          .Multi-canal BPPV
                                             • Can occur on both sides - primarily from head trauma (Katsarkas A, 1999)
                                             • Can occur in multiple canals in the same side
                                             • General rule is to treat one canal per visit
                                          .Vestibular agnosia: nystagmus without symptoms
                                          .Subjective BPPV: symptoms without nystagmus
                                          .Conversion of probable to definitive BPPV
                                       ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                       .BPPV.1.Dix-Hallpike ('Dix-Hallpike test.mp4') ('Dix-Hallpike test.mp4')
                                          ΓGenerals
                                             (Γ).Before conducting positional tests, assess cervical ROM
                                                 • Only one case report (Moore P et al, 2018) in literature that Dix-Hallpike has resulted in symptoms consistent with Vertebral Basilar Insufficiency
                                                 • Tests for VBI are not reliable, but still a good idea to assess cervical ROM to see if you need to modify positioning
                                                 • If neck range of motion is limited, tilt head of table down
                                             (Γ).Head shaking during the Dix-Hallpike
                                                • Can improve the chance of a positive Dix-Hallpike by 15% in posterior canal BPPV
                                                • Consider as an option if all positional tests are negative but history strongly suggests BPPV
                                             ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                             • Turn the head 45 degrees toward the side being assessed
                                             • Bring the patient into a supine position with 20- 30 degrees extension over the edge of the bed
                                             ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                             .Observing nystagmus
                                                 • In posterior canal BPPV, nystagmus is provoked following Dix Hallpike positioning with the affected ear down  
                                                 • Nystagmus will be torsional and upbeating
                                                 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                                   .Characteristics of the nystagmus in the Dix-Hallpike
                                                       • In posterior canal BPPV, torsional and upbeating nystagmus is provoked by the Dix-Hallpike test
                                                       • There is a latency period between assuming supine position and the onset of the nystagmus and vertigo symptoms
                                                       • The vertigo and nystagmus increase in severity and then resolve within 60 seconds of the onset (crescendo-decrescendo nystagmus)

                                                       • If the anterior canal is involved, can observe torsional downbeating nystagmus
                                                           HOWEVER: The observation of downbeating positional nystagmus requires careful assessment to rule out brainstem or cerebellar lesions
                                          ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                          .BPPV.2.Loaded Dix-Hallpike
                                             • Head is turned 45 degrees to the side being tested
                                             • Flex the head down by 30 degrees (loading the posterior canal)
                                             • Then the clinician helps the patient into supine and extends the head 20-30 degrees
                                             • Goal is to maximize the response of the otoconia moving through the canal
                                          .BPPV.3.Modified Dix-Hallpike Test With Head Over Pillow
                                             • Sensitivity: 96%
                                             • Specificity: 88%
                                          .BPPV.4.Sidelying Test
                                             • Start in short sitting in the middle of a treatment table
                                             • Turn the head 45 degrees away from the side being tested
                                             • Help the patient into sidelying (this is the side you are testing)
                                             • Observe for nystagmus
                                             • Sensitivity: 90%
                                             • Specificity: 75%

                                    IV.Posterior Canal Canalith Repositioning Maneuvers Γ(INTERVENTIONS)
                                       Γ.Generals
                                          .Treatment for Posterior Canal BPPV
                                              • Treat or refer to a clinician who can treat with a canalith repositioning maneuver
                                                  • Strong Recommendation by CPG
                                              • These manuevers work by freeing the otoconia from the cupula (cupulolithiasis) and/or by moving the otoconia out of the involved semicircular canal back into the otolith organs
                                                  • Effective in 91% of cases (compared to sham maneuver 46% effective)
                                       ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                       .PCCRM.1.Modified Epley ('Modified Epley Maneuver.mp4')
                                           • Turn the head 45 degrees to the affected side
                                           • Move the patient into supine and extend the head 20-30 degrees [Dix Hallpike]
                                           • Wait until the nystagmus resolves plus 30 seconds
                                           • Turn the head 90 degrees toward the unaffected side
                                           • Wait until the nystagmus resolves plus 30 seconds
                                           • Help the patient to roll onto the unaffected side with the head looking toward the floor
                                           • Wait until the nystagmus resolves plus 30 seconds
                                           • Carefully help the patient to sit up and HOLD ONTO THE PATIENT
                                       .PCCRM.2.Semont ('Semont & Maneuver.mp4')
                                       .PCCRM.3.Semont Plus
                                          • Start in short sitting in the middle of the bed
                                          • Turn the head 45 degrees away from the affected side
                                          • Help the patient to lay onto the affected side with the head extended over the bed 60 degrees
                                          • Wait until nystagmus resolves plus 30 seconds
                                          • Quickly move the patient from the affected side to the unaffected side (within 1.5 seconds)
                                          • Wait until nystagmus resolves plus 30 seconds
                                          • Slowly sit the patient up and hold on for safety
                                          • No difference between treatment with the modified Epley maneuver vs the Semont plus maneuver
                                       .PCCRM.4.Li Maneuver ('Li Maneuver.mp4')
                                          • For right posterior canal BPPV (Li et al 2017)
                                          • There was no difference between the Epley and the Li maneuver (n=120) in their randomized trial

                                    V.Horizontal Canal BPPV Positional Tests Γ(TESTS)
                                       Γ.General
                                          • Otoconia are displaced into the horizontal canal 
                                          • Canalithiasis: otoconia are freely floating in the canal
                                          • Cupulolithiasis: otoconia are adhered to the cupula within the canal
                                          • Horizontal canal prevalence: 8-17% of BPPV cases
                                          ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                          .Horizontal Canal BPPV nystagmus characteristics
                                             • Directional Changing Positional Nystagmus 
                                             • Geotropic or ageotropic (apogeotropic) nystagmus associated with vertigo in the supine roll test (both sides)
                                                 • Geotropic: fast phase of the nystagmus beats toward the earth (typically transient)
                                                 • Apogeotropic: fast phase of the nystagmus beats away from the earth (typically persistent)
                                          .Determining the affected side
                                              • Geotropic type
                                                  • When rolling to the affected side, nystagmus (and symptoms) will be more intense
                                                  • When rolling to the unaffected side, nystagmus (and symptoms) will be less intense
                                              • Apogeotropic type
                                                  • When rolling to the affected side, nystagmus (and symptoms) will be less intense
                                                  • When rolling to the unaffected side, nystagmus (and symptoms) will be more intense
                                              • Sometimes it can be difficult to determine the intensity of nystagmus and symptoms
                                       ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                       .HC-BPPV-PT.1.(2º)Long Sit to Supine
                                          .Sit to supine test
                                              • PROCEDURE:
                                                  • Patient begins long sitting on mat
                                                  • Patient is quickly brought into the supine position with the head flexed 30°
                                              • FINDINGS:
                                                  • Evokes nystagmus towards the healthy side in geotropic forms (Geotropic=Good)
                                                  • Evokes nystagmus towards the affected side in apogeotropic forms Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences Vol. 1164, 1Basic and Clinical (Apogeotropic=Affected)
                                       .HC-BPPV-PT.2.(3º)Roll Test (Pagnini-McClure Roll Test) ('Roll test with sit to supine test.mp4')
                                          .Supine roll test
                                             • If the history is consistent with BPPV and the Dix-Hallpike test exhibits horizontal or no nystagmus, the supine roll test should be performed to assess for lateral canal BPPV (Recommended by CPG)
                                             • Position the patient in supine with head neutral
                                             • Rotate the head 90 degrees to one side and observe for nystagmus
                                             • Bring the head back to neutral and wait until nystagmus has subsided
                                             • Rotate the head 90 degrees in the opposite direction and observe for nystagmus
                                       .HC-BPPV-PT.3.(1º)Bow and Lean Test ('Bow and Lean test.mp4')
                                          .Bow and Lean Test
                                              Sit erect
                                                  • If geotropic, beats towards healthy ear (Geotropic=Good)
                                                  • If apogeotropic, beats towards affected ear (Apogeotropic=Affected)
                                              Sit erect and bend head 60° forward
                                                  • If geotropic, beats towards affected ear
                                                  • If apogeotropic, beats 
                                                  towards healthy ear
                                              Sit erect and bend head backwards  
                                                  • If geotropic, beats towards healthy ear (Geotropic=Good)
                                                  • If apogeotropic, beats towards affected ear (Apogeotropic=Affected)

                                    VI.Horizontal Canal Canalith Repositioning Maneuvers Γ(INTERVENTIONS)
                                       Γ.General
                                          .Treatment for HC BPPV
                                             Geotropic Type 
                                                 • Gufoni (for geotropic)
                                                 • Li Quick
                                                 • Lempert (barbeque) Roll
                                             Apogeotropic Type
                                                 • Gufoni (for apogeotropic)
                                                 • Kim
                                       ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                       .Geotropic
                                          .HC-CCRM.1.Barbecue Maneuver for Canalithiasis
                                             .Lempert (Barbeque) Roll maneuver (!!).No ho entenc; No se que passa amb l'otoconia
                                                 • Start in the supine position
                                                 • Rotate the head (or roll body) 90 degrees to the affected side
                                                 • Rotate back to supine head neutral
                                                 • Roll onto the unaffected side
                                                 • Roll into prone, head in neutral
                                                 • To resume sitting, the patient can either roll onto the affected side or sit up from prone
                                                 • Should wait until the nystagmus stops plus 30 seconds between each position

                                                 ('')
                                                     When it is determined to be horizontal canal BPPV affecting the right side, the patient is taken through a series of step-wise 90-degree tums away from the affected side in Steps 1 through 5, holding each position for 10 to 30 seconds. From Step 5, the patient positions his or her bod,' to the back (6) in preparation for the rapid and simultaneous movement from the eupire face up to tie sitting position (7).
                                          .HC-CCRM.2.Gufoni Maneuver for Canalithiasis ('Gufoni Maneuver Geotropic.mp4')
                                             .Gufoni Maneuver for Geotropic Type Horizontal Canal BPPV
                                                 • Start in a short sitting position in the center of a table
                                                 • The patient’s head is then quickly 
                                                 • Help the patient into sidelying onto the unaffected side (head neutral) for 30 seconds turned toward the ground 45-60 degrees
                                                 • Hold the position for 2 minutes
                                                 • Help the patient to sit up with the head turned toward the unaffected side
                                                 • Hold onto the patient for safety
                                          .HC-CCRM.3.Li Quick Maneuver for Canalithiasis ('Li for canalithiasis.mp4')
                                             .Li Quick maneuver for HC BPPV (geotropic)
                                                 • Start in supine 
                                                 • Roll onto affected side and remain until symptoms stop
                                                 • Roll patient quickly to the unaffected sidelying position 
                                                 • Remain for 2 minutes
                                                 • Then bring them to sitting
                                                 • Total time: ~ 3 minutes
                                                 • In their study of 120 patients with HC BPPV, Li et al. found the Li Quick maneuver to have similar efficacy to the barbeque roll maneuver (93% vs 91% resolved in 1 week)
                                       .Ageotropic
                                          .HC-CCRM.4.Gufoni Maneuver for Cupulolithiasis ('Gufoni Maneuver Apogeotropic.mp4')
                                             .Gufoni maneuver for Apogeotropic HC BPPV ('') ← See images
                                          .HC-CCRM.5.Kim Maneuver for Cupulolithiasis ('Kim for cupulolithiasis.mp4')
                                             .Cupulolith Repositioning Maneuver for Apogeotropic HC BPPV ('') ← See images to understand
                                                • Goal: 
                                                    • To move debris located on side of cupula adjacent to utricular vestibule (4th position) or to long arm (1st position) into the vestibule
                                                • Procedure:
                                                    • Each position maintained 3 minutes.
                                                    • Vibration applied for 30s 1st and 4th position.
                                                    • Activity Restrictions: Sleep on uninvolved side
                                                • Success Rate 97.4% (76/78) after 2 repetitions of maneuver
                                    Γ.Final Considerations
                                       (Γ).Post-repositioning instructions
                                           • Original Epley maneuver included strict post-repositioning instructions
                                           • However, there is now high levels of evidence that have found that post-repositioning instructions do not improve clinical outcomes
                                           • Clinicians should NOT recommend postprocedural restrictions after CRM for BPPV
                                               • Strong recommendation by CPG
                                           • Benefits of no post-repositioning instructions:
                                               • Patient can return to normal lifestyle/activities
                                               • Reduced anxiety
                                               • Less sleep interruption
                                               • More comfort/quality of life

                                       (Γ).What happens if the symptoms do not resolve after CRM
                                          • Try again – it is not uncommon to need more than 1 visit to be successful
                                          • Try a different CRM if one is not successful
                                          • Assess the other canals – could be multi-canal involvement
                                          • Refer to a vestibular rehabilitation expert
                                          • Refer back to physician if BPPV persists

                                       (Γ).Response to canalith repositioning maneuvers
                                          • Canal conversion in 6-7% of posterior canal cases of BPPV treated with CRM
                                          • Sensation of falling within 30 minutes of the maneuver
                                          • Nausea, vomiting
                                          • Postural instability that can last 24 hours

                                       (Γ).Systematic review and meta-analysis of BPPV outcomes in young versus older adults (Sim E et al, 2019)
                                          • Take home message: after you treat the BPPV, complete a thorough balance, gait, and functional assessment (particularly among older adults)

                                       (Γ).Patient Education after CRM
                                           • Diagnosis of BPPV
                                           • Common signs and symptoms of BPPV
                                           • Even after successful treatment
                                               • May experience imbalance after the repositioning
                                               • May be sensitive to motion/movement after repositioning
                                           • Follow-up in the clinic to reassess and further assess balance and gait
                                           • BPPV recurrence
                                           • Return to regular activities

                        • May also include a screen of other cranial nerves

                     Let's make a pause.
